# Synthetic fixture

`minimal-pe-x64.exe` is generated byte-for-byte by `python3 tests/make_minimal_pe.py`. It is a minimal PE32+ x86-64 image used to exercise static parsing and report generation. It contains a `RET` byte and padding, has no symbol table, and is not a real-world executable or benchmark.

`compiler-generated-x64.exe` is a checked-in freestanding PE32+ x86-64 executable built from [`compiler-generated-x64.c`](compiler-generated-x64.c) with Clang 18.1.3 and LLD 18.1.3. The source file records the exact compile and link commands. Gate 1 asserts its export, entry point, instruction bytes/addresses, and Capstone detail. The fixture is only parsed statically by the tests; it is never launched.

`make_phase1_fixture.py` creates additional small deterministic synthetic images for malformed/truncated decoding, bounded metadata, CLR, and alternate-machine cases. They are generated into a temporary directory during tests and likewise never executed.

`realworld/sqlite3-3.54.0-x64.dll` is a hash-verified, official SQLite public-domain Windows x64 DLL used as a static-only Gate 5 corpus input. Its upstream source, published archive checksum, extracted-file hash, license basis, and explicit unknown compiler metadata are recorded in [`realworld/README.md`](realworld/README.md) and `tests/benchmarks/v1/phase5-corpus.json`. Its executable code exceeds the current report-record budget; Gate 5 records decoded and limit-excluded byte counts separately. No fixture is launched.
